historyReviewBoundary: All 115 histories have author source checks. Final independent review covered metadata and numerical checks for all 115 classes, 12 deeper class targets and source-gap samples in seven classes. It did not independently verify every passage of every cited source.

history.name: DPP-4 inhibitors

starting.description: After GLP-1 had been observed to stimulate insulin secretion and show therapeutic promise, investigators identified DPP-4-mediated cleavage of GLP-1 and GIP in enzyme and serum experiments. In the Sandoz account this observation prompted a proposal to inhibit DPP-4 and preserve physiological incretin action.

inspiration.description: Endogenous GLP-1's insulin-related physiology and its experimentally observed enzymatic cleavage inspired DPP-4 inhibition in the documented programs. The same experiments showed cleavage of GIP; the Sandoz account predicted that inhibition could also protect GIP. Merck additionally cited clinical observations of glucose lowering by administered GLP-1. The therapeutic inhibitors were deliberately developed small molecules, not required to share the hormones' chemical structures.

steps.description: In purified-enzyme and human-serum experiments DPP-4 cleaved GLP-1 and GIP, and enzyme inhibitors prevented production of serum cleavage fragments.

According to the Sandoz/Novartis account the enzyme observation prompted a proposal to inhibit DPP-4 to preserve physiological GLP-1; an existing inhibitor was evaluated and optimized into DPP-728 and vildagliptin.
A 2002 four-week placebo-controlled human study reported improved glucose control with DPP-728; it was not designed to establish the mechanism of benefit.

In a parallel program begun in 1999, Merck used prior human GLP-1 and animal inhibitor evidence to choose the target, screened active compounds, and optimized a piperazine-related series into sitagliptin.

A separate program screened for DPP-4 inhibition and optimized an active xanthine scaffold into BI 1356, linagliptin, representing a different chemical route within the established incretin-protection concept.

design.description: Researchers screened and optimized small-molecule inhibitors, creating chemically distinct inhibitors including DPP-728, sitagliptin and xanthine-based linagliptin. In the sitagliptin series they introduced fused piperazine replacements to address metabolism and later improved oral absorption; in the linagliptin series they changed substituents to improve potency and reduce hERG-channel and M1-receptor interactions. These chemical inventions do not erase the observation-led target rationale.

circumstances.description: The Sandoz team's selection and testing of valine pyrrolidide as a DPP-4 inhibitor was a purposeful test of the incretin-protection hypothesis; this does not characterize every earlier observation as planned or unexpected.

limits: The Sandoz, Merck and linagliptin reports document different development programs using the established physiological concept; the Merck account is not evidence of first invention of the class.

Linagliptin's xanthine screening lead is chemically distinct from the sitagliptin series and the Sandoz valine-pyrrolidide lead; this account does not reconstruct every analogue or decide chemical-lead priority.
conflicts: Foley and Ahrén describe GLP-1 degradation as solely due to DPP-4; Mentlein and colleagues' original conclusions concern the main enzyme in their human-serum conditions, not universal exclusivity.

Foley and Ahrén say GLP-1 and GIP share their first five N-terminal residues, whereas the sequences shown in Mentlein et al. Figure 1 differ at the first residue. Both have alanine in the second position from the N terminus in the forms tested.
gaps: Early animal proof-of-concept reports cited by the retrospectives have not been read directly; the 1993 serum experiment and a 2002 human DPP-728 trial were read.
Sandoz's attribution of the 1993 proposal is retrospective and partly based on personal communication; competing independent program priority is not adjudicated.

humanContributionInterpretation.summary: Human GLP-1 infusion results and preclinical DPP4 evidence jointly supported Merck's inhibitor program.
humanContributionInterpretation.scope: Deliberate human experiments and an existing laboratory hypothesis, not a new incidental patient observation.
